# RSM-MSBA on a NixOS server (multi-user)

> **The goal:** one server, where every student logs in over **VS Code
> Remote-SSH** and gets the *same* computing environment — most of the benefits
> of Docker + Kubernetes (a consistent image, isolation by account, atomic
> rollback) using **only NixOS**, no containers and no orchestrator.

The key idea: the server does **not** redefine the environment. It **consumes**
the `rsm-nix` flake as an input and puts `rsm-setup` on every student's PATH. The
toolchain is byte-for-byte what students run on their laptops, maintained in one
place. NixOS adds only *host* concerns — accounts, SSH, storage, the firewall.

A deployable, copy-pasteable version of everything below lives in the repo under
[`nixos/`](https://github.com/radiant-ai-hub/rsm-nix/tree/main/nixos). This page
explains the design; that directory is what you actually put in `/etc/nixos`.

## What you get (and don't)

| Container/k8s feature | NixOS equivalent here |
|---|---|
| Identical image for everyone | The shared `rsm-nix` flake, pinned by `flake.lock` |
| Isolation between users | Separate Linux accounts + `/home`; no sudo for students |
| Atomic deploy + rollback | `nixos-rebuild switch` / `--rollback` (bootable generations) |
| Declarative config | `configuration.nix` + `students.nix` in git |
| Resource limits / scheduling | **Deferred** (see the end) — systemd slices add this later |

It is *not* a scheduler and (for the alpha) does not cap per-user CPU/RAM. That
is a deliberate, documented next step, not an oversight.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

- A machine running **NixOS** (this is Path B; the Ubuntu + Nix route is
  [server-ubuntu-nix.md](server-ubuntu-nix.md)).
- Admin (sudo) access and the students' **SSH public keys**.
- Flakes enabled (the config below turns them on).

---

## 2. The files

Copy these from [`nixos/`](https://github.com/radiant-ai-hub/rsm-nix/tree/main/nixos)
into `/etc/nixos`:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `flake.nix` | System flake: pins `nixpkgs` + the `rsm-nix` input → `nixosConfigurations.<host>`. |
| `configuration.nix` | Host glue: hostname, boot loader, Nix daemon, locale, `stateVersion`. |
| `rsm-server.nix` | The reusable RSM module (everything in §3). |
| `students.nix` | Account registry — copied from `students.nix.example`, with real keys. |

`flake.nix` wires it together and consumes the environment flake:

```nix
inputs = {
  nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
  rsm-nix.url = "github:radiant-ai-hub/rsm-nix";   # the student/dev environment
};
outputs = { self, nixpkgs, rsm-nix, ... }: {
  nixosConfigurations.rsm-server = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
    system = "x86_64-linux";
    specialArgs = { inherit rsm-nix; };
    modules = [ ./configuration.nix ./rsm-server.nix ./students.nix ];
  };
};
```

> We deliberately let `rsm-nix` use its **own pinned nixpkgs** (no
> `follows`), so the env stays identical to the laptop build. The cost is a
> second, cached nixpkgs eval — worth it for reproducibility.

---

## 3. The RSM module, decision by decision

All of this is in `nixos/rsm-server.nix`.

### 3.1 nix-ld — the VS Code Remote-SSH fix (most important)

VS Code's "server" downloads its own dynamically-linked Node binary. On NixOS
there is no `/lib64/ld-linux-*.so` for it to use, so without help Remote-SSH
connects and immediately drops. `nix-ld` supplies a standard loader plus common
libraries:

```nix
programs.nix-ld.enable = true;
programs.nix-ld.libraries = with pkgs; [
  stdenv.cc.cc zlib glib openssl curl icu util-linux
];
```

This is the single change most likely to be missing from a hand-rolled config.

### 3.2 SSH (key-only) + firewall

```nix
services.openssh.enable = true;
services.openssh.settings = {
  PasswordAuthentication = false;
  KbdInteractiveAuthentication = false;
  AllowTcpForwarding = true;        # forward pgweb / Postgres to the laptop
};
networking.firewall.allowedTCPPorts = [ 22 ];   # only SSH is exposed
```

Per-student databases are reached through SSH port-forwarding, never published
on the network.

### 3.3 No `wheel` for students (security)

On a shared box students must **not** have sudo. In `students.nix` they get only
the `rsm` group; keep a *separate* admin account with `wheel` (or you lock
yourself out of `nixos-rebuild`):

```nix
extraGroups = [ "rsm" ];          # students: NO "wheel"
```

### 3.4 Shared uv cache (disk)

One uv env is ~1.2 GB **plus** ~1.2 GB of downloads. Per student that adds up
fast. Because `rsm-nix` runs uv in **copy** link-mode, each student's venv gets
private copies — only the *downloads* can be shared safely:

```nix
users.groups.rsm = { };
systemd.tmpfiles.rules = [
  "d /srv/uv-cache 2775 root rsm - -"               # setgid: new files inherit group rsm
  "a+ /srv/uv-cache - - - - d:g:rsm:rwx,g:rsm:rwx"  # default ACL: group-writable regardless of umask
];
environment.sessionVariables.UV_CACHE_DIR = "/srv/uv-cache";
```

`rsm-nix/bin/rsm-env.sh` already honors an inherited `UV_CACHE_DIR`, so this Just
Works. (If uv ever complains about permissions across users, drop the shared dir
and fall back to the per-user default — correctness over disk.)

### 3.5 Per-user Postgres port

Every student's `rsm-pg-start` would otherwise bind `127.0.0.1:8765` — a
collision on one host. This is handled in the environment itself, not the NixOS
config: `rsm-nix/bin/rsm-env.sh` defaults `PGPORT` to `8765 + (uid % 1000)`, so
each user gets a distinct port. Because the env header is sourced by every entry
point (login *and* non-login shells, the dev shell, and the `rsm-pg-*` wrappers),
the port is consistent everywhere — unlike a `profile.d` snippet, which only
login shells read.

(The unix socket used by `rsm-pg-psql` is already per-user and never collides;
this covers the TCP listener and `pgweb`. For very large cohorts, `% 1000` could
theoretically collide — assign explicit ports then.)

### 3.6 direnv, system-wide

```nix
programs.direnv = { enable = true; nix-direnv.enable = true; };
```

This is the fix for "direnv: command not found" inside VS Code terminals: every
login shell gets the hook, so `~/rsm-msba` (and course subfolders) activate on
`cd`.

### 3.7 Workspace seeding (the real flake, not a template)

A `oneshot` unit clones `rsm-nix` into each student's `~/rsm-nix` if missing —
the real flake is the only source of truth. Students then run `rsm-setup` once to
build their personal env. No toy template, no `cp -r` blueprint:

```nix
systemd.services.rsm-seed-workspaces = {
  wantedBy = [ "multi-user.target" ];
  wants = [ "network-online.target" ]; after = [ "network-online.target" ];
  path = [ pkgs.git pkgs.coreutils pkgs.getent ];   # getent lives in glibc, not coreutils
  serviceConfig = {
    Type = "oneshot"; RemainAfterExit = true;
    Environment = "GIT_SSL_CAINFO=${pkgs.cacert}/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt";
  };
  script = ''
    for u in $(getent group rsm | cut -d: -f4 | tr ',' ' '); do
      home="$(getent passwd "$u" | cut -d: -f6)"
      [ -e "$home/rsm-nix/flake.nix" ] || \
        git clone https://github.com/radiant-ai-hub/rsm-nix.git "$home/rsm-nix" && \
        chown -R "$u":rsm "$home/rsm-nix"
    done
  '';
};
```

### 3.8 Atomic rollback (the headline safety net)

`environment.systemPackages` puts `git`, `direnv`, and `rsm-msba.packages.<sys>.rsm-setup`
on PATH. The Nix daemon is configured with flakes + `auto-optimise-store` + weekly
GC. Every `nixos-rebuild switch` is a new **bootable generation**; if a change
breaks the box, `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --rollback` (or selecting the prior
generation at boot) restores it instantly. That is the k8s-style "roll back the
deployment" guarantee, built in.

---

## 4. Deploy

```bash
# On the host, as admin:
cd /etc/nixos
# bring in flake.nix, configuration.nix, rsm-server.nix
sudo nixos-generate-config                # real hardware-configuration.nix
cp students.nix.example students.nix      # then edit: usernames + real keys
# set networking.hostName, nixosConfigurations.<name>, and
# system.stateVersion (= this machine's install release) to match
nix develop github:radiant-ai-hub/rsm-nix -c true   # pre-warm the store (optional)
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake /etc/nixos#<host>
```

If anything goes wrong: `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --rollback`.

---

## 5. Per-student first run

After the switch, each student (from a laptop):

1. **VS Code → Remote-SSH** to `<user>@<host>` (install the *Remote - SSH* and
   *direnv* extensions).
2. In a remote terminal: `cd ~ && nix develop ~/rsm-nix -c rsm-setup` (the seed
   unit already cloned `~/rsm-nix`). This builds their nix-uv env, the
   "Python (nix-uv)" kernel, and course folders — a few minutes the first time.
3. **Open Folder → `~/rsm-msba`**. Terminals and notebooks pick up the env via
   direnv; choose the **Python (nix-uv)** kernel for notebooks.

---

## 6. Validate

```bash
# as a student account:
cd ~/rsm-msba
python examples/check_environment.py     # expect: ALL GOOD
rsm-pg-start && rsm-pg-psql -c '\l'      # Postgres on the per-user PGPORT
```

Then confirm two accounts can run `rsm-pg-start` **at the same time** without a
port clash, and that a second student's `rsm-setup` is fast (shared
`/srv/uv-cache` hit).

---

## 7. Deferred past the alpha

These are intentionally **out of scope** for a 4-user alpha; the design leaves a
clean place for each:

- **Per-user resource limits** (the one real container feature missing): systemd
  `user-.slice` with `MemoryMax` / `MemoryHigh` / `CPUQuota`, plus
  `systemd-oomd`, so one runaway job can't starve the box.
- **Disk quotas** on `/home` (e.g. `fileSystems` `usrquota` + `quota` service).
- **Account automation / SSO** — replace the hand-written `students.nix` with an
  `AuthorizedKeysCommand` or a generated registry once the roster grows.
- **Local binary cache / substituter** — for a large cohort, to avoid every
  machine pulling from `cache.nixos.org`.
- **GPU/CUDA** — `hardware.nvidia` + an optional PyTorch layer.

Add them incrementally; none change the environment definition, only the host.
